messages:
Priya Singh: @channel seeing a sharp spike in client paging errors right after the v3.9.2 rollout. Canary shows ~40% 4xx on /v1/paging/stream and a handful of production customers reporting partial responses. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout v3.9.2 -> health degraded at 2364509700, rolling window error rate 42%. Auto-canary pause engaged.

Jamie Wu: I'm oncall — taking this. Priya, can you paste the earliest failing logs and any recent schema changes in the SDK?

Priya Singh: Copying logs snippet below. Noticed schema field `page_token_v2` added in SDK v3.9.2 that some legacy clients don't accept.

```
ERROR 2364509721 service=paging svc_req_id=abc123 client=client-sdk/2.7.4 status=400 "invalid page_token"
WARN 2364509722 service=paging decode_error token_bytes=0
TRACE 2364509730 service=router trace_id=xyz789 route=/v1/paging/stream handler=paging-handler
```

Alex Carter: Confirming: packaging changed the token encoding to include a small header. It was behind a feature flag in SDK but rollout toggled it on for canary. Some older clients (2.x) don't understand the header -> 400.

Lee Morgan: Customer impact: top 5 customers account for ~60% of paging traffic. Telemetry shows messages truncated for 12% of requests overall, concentrated in NA region.

Samir Patel: @Jamie what mitigation can we do immediately? Rolling back is an option but we have partial traffic already. Can we flip a server-side compatibility shim?

Jamie Wu: Options: 1) Flip kill-switch feature flag for the new token header (server-side parse fallback) — fast. 2) Rollback canary -> slower but cleans state. 3) Hotpatch router to accept both token formats. I'll try the kill-switch first.

Jamie Wu: Running kill-switch now: `rctrl feature kill token_v2_header --env=prod --scope=canary`

incident-bot: Feature flag "token_v2_header" toggled OFF for canary at 2364509850 by Jamie Wu.

Priya Singh: After the flag flip, canary 4xx dropped to ~9% within 2 mins. Some clients still failing due to cached bad tokens.

Alex Carter: I'm deploying a parser fallback to the router (non-breaking) as a hotpatch: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> `a4c3d2`. Pushing a small shim that will attempt legacy decode on 400.

Lee Morgan: Customer comms: support already opened tickets for CustomerA and CustomerB. SLA risk low but visible user errors. Recommend banner to status page: "Intermittent paging errors for some clients — mitigation in progress."

Samir Patel: Jamie, do we want to do a full rollback of v3.9.2 after the shim? If the release toggled other unrelated behavior, safer to rollback.

Jamie Wu: Agreed. Start staged rollback for the canary and pause rollout. I'll coordinate with Releases.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for v3.9.2 canary -> target release v3.9.1 at 2364509990.

Priya Singh: Monitoring: error rate trending down. Post-shim + rollback, global 4xx now ~1.8%. NA region back to baseline.

Alex Carter: Hotpatch router shim merged and live at 2364510305. Code snippet:

```
// router decode fallback
try {
  token = decodeV2(header);
} catch (e) {
  token = tryLegacyDecode(raw);
}
```

Jamie Wu: Handover to next oncall: @Alex, Priya — you're owners for the next 4 hours to watch for reoccurrence. I'll stay on until the rollback finishes and customer tickets are updated.

Priya Singh: Filed short postmortem runbook card: "Paging token schema drift during v3.9.2 rollout" -> includes root cause, timeline, and action items.

Lee Morgan: Action items assigned:
- Alex: revert SDK packaging step that enabled header by default + add compatibility test (due EOD)
- Priya: update status page and follow up with affected customers (ongoing)
- Samir: add automated pre-rollout client-compat smoke tests (P1)
- Jamie: draft incident timeline and coordinate postmortem meeting (tomorrow 1400 UTC)

Samir Patel: One note: add a check in the deployment pipeline that ensures no client-compat-change flips without an explicit opt-in and compatibility runway.

incident-bot: Incident channel updated: severity=SEV3 (partial user impact) at 2364510600.

Priya Singh: Final check: last failing ticket cleared at 2364511600, rollback completed at 2364511550. Will monitor for 24h. Thanks all for the quick turnaround. :raised_hands:

Jamie Wu: Closing thread — we'll reconvene in the postmortem. Good mitigation work.
